description: Imports Mailchimp Marketing audiences, members, segments, tags, interests, campaigns, automations and per-recipient email engagement activity.

placeholders.dc: Resolved once at connector startup by `resolve_base_url`, differently per credential mode. API Key mode: the substring after the FINAL '-' of the key itself (rpartition); a key with no suffix raises a user-facing ValidationError. OAuth mode: the connector GETs https://login.mailchimp.com/oauth2/metadata with the access token and uses the returned `api_endpoint` verbatim, appending '/3.0' — so in that mode the whole origin, not just {dc}, comes from the lookup.

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment: the literal `/3.0` at the end of the base URL. No version header or query param is sent.

continuity.ourSideLoss: Nothing is lost by pausing: every incremental leg is a server-side time-window filter (`since_*`/`before_*`, or `since` for email-activity) anchored on our own checkpoint, so a longer pause simply widens the next window. Two soft edges exist. (1) `email_activity`'s dedup suppression lives in the CDK's in-process `emitted_changes_cache`, so a restart re-emits events inside the 10-minute lookback — duplicates only, and the collection key absorbs them. (2) `campaigns` is filtered on `create_time`, which never changes, so campaign mutations that occur while paused are never observed by the incremental leg at all; only the daily cron re-backfill recovers them.
continuity.resumeWindow: unbounded — no server-side retention window is consumed
continuity.notes: Pure poll-mode HTTP connector. It creates no slot, publication, subscription, scratch table, consumer group, webhook, or batch job on Mailchimp's side — every request is a plain GET. Nothing accrues on the customer's infra between cron ticks. Parent IDs (list ids) are re-resolved from `/lists` on every connector startup, and `_patch_missing_subtask_states` seeds fresh per-list subtasks for lists created while we were stopped, so a long gap does not orphan new lists.

configFields.name: start_date
configFields.description: UTC date and time in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Data generated before this is not replicated. Defaults to 30 days before the present. Bounds every backfill window and the email-activity `since`.

configFields.name: credentials.api_key
configFields.description: Required when the 'API Key' authentication variant is selected. Mailchimp API key including its data center suffix (e.g. ends in -us21); the suffix after the final '-' becomes the {dc} of the base URL and a key without one is rejected at validation. Sent as HTTP Basic with an empty, non-user-supplied username.

configFields.name: credentials.client_id
configFields.description: Required when the 'OAuth Credentials' variant is selected. Standalone the user must register their own Mailchimp OAuth app; Estuary's hosted control plane instead fills this from its pre-registered provider ('x-oauth2-provider': 'mailchimp').

configFields.name: credentials.client_secret
configFields.description: Required when the 'OAuth Credentials' variant is selected. Same provenance as client_id.

configFields.name: credentials.access_token
configFields.description: Required when the 'OAuth Credentials' variant is selected. Mailchimp issues a single non-expiring access token and no refresh token, so this is the durable secret (the CDK's LongLivedClientCredentialsOAuth2Credentials shape) and is replayed as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' on every request without any refresh exchange. With this variant the data center comes from the OAuth metadata endpoint, not from the token.

authTierRationale: The easiest mode offered is a single self-serve Mailchimp API key pasted into one field and sent over HTTP Basic with an empty username — no app registration, no token exchange, and the data center is derived from the key itself. The OAuth mode is materially harder standalone and is scored T3_BYO_REFRESH: its config schema requires client_id, client_secret AND access_token, so outside Estuary's hosted control plane the user must register their own Mailchimp OAuth app and complete the authorization-code exchange themselves. Mailchimp issues no refresh token, so the long-lived access_token occupies the slot T3 normally reserves for a refresh token — the user work is the same shape (bring a durable token), which is why it is scored T3 rather than T2. Estuary ships a pre-registered provider ('x-oauth2-provider': 'mailchimp'), so inside their hosted UI the OAuth mode is effectively one click; that is a control-plane property, not a property of this connector.

unionMisfits.description: The OAuth mode is two different things at two different times and the union forces a choice. At CONFIG time it is an authorization_code flow (authUrl/tokenUrl/accessTokenBody templates in OAUTH2_SPEC, response mapped as {access_token: /access_token}). At REQUEST time there is no flow at all: the CDK's TokenSource returns ('Bearer', credentials.access_token) verbatim for LongLivedClientCredentialsOAuth2Credentials, with no expiry tracking and no refresh exchange — it is a static bearer header. Encoded here as oauth2 because the T3 tier only makes sense with the flow described, but a consumer that expects to run a token refresh against tokenUrl at runtime would be wrong.

The basic scheme requires a usernameField, but there is no user-supplied username: ApiKey hides it from the config schema (SkipJsonSchema) and hardcodes it to the empty string, so the header is base64(':<api_key>'). Recorded as "" for shape conformance only — a UI that renders usernameField as a form input would produce a field the user must be told to leave blank.

configFields is a flat list, but `credentials` is a Pydantic discriminated one-of on `credentials_title` with two mutually exclusive branches ('API Key' vs 'OAuth Credentials'). Every field inside a branch is required WITHIN that branch and forbidden outside it; flattening loses both facts, so all five credential fields are recorded required:false with the branch named in the description. The discriminator field itself (credentials.credentials_title) is omitted entirely.

STILL A MISFIT in v2. list_members is not one request with a params map: it is TWO independent sweeps per list (bare, and status=archived), each registered as its own CDK subtask with its own incremental cursor and its own frozen backfill window. The sweeps' cursors must stay independent — a member unarchived between two sweeps of a shared-cursor walk would be missed until its next change. `pull.backfill`/`pull.incremental` gave us the leg split we needed for other streams, but there is still no axis for 'walk this same leg N times with different filters and N independent cursors'. Recorded as a described placeholder in `status` rather than a literal.

email_activity is doubly derived and the emitted document is not the paginated item. (a) Each leg first drains /reports with a fields projection and applies a recency gate before touching any campaign — a filtering pre-request that pathPlaceholders can describe but not model. (b) recordsPath 'emails' names the ENVELOPE key: each emails[] item is a recipient row carrying a nested activity[] array, and the connector emits one flattened document per (recipient, event), dissolving the recipient row into _meta. A consumer treating recordsPath as the document path would emit ~1 doc per recipient instead of ~1 per event. (c) The incremental leg rewinds `since` by a 10-minute lookback and relies on an in-process dedup cache to suppress the overlap, and drops events with timestamp > horizon client-side; the endpoint has no `before`-style upper bound.

proposedShape.upperBound: client-side filter on horizon; no server-side before-param exists

unionMisfits.description: campaigns carries TWO schedules at once and the union holds one. Its resourceConfig is {interval: PT5M, schedule: '0 0 * * *'}: the interval drives the incremental poll, and the cron independently triggers a full re-backfill. The cron is not an alternative to the interval, it is a second axis — and here it is load-bearing rather than cosmetic, because /campaigns only exposes a create_time filter, so campaign MUTATIONS are invisible to the incremental leg and are recovered solely by that nightly re-backfill. Recorded as the interval; the cron is lost.

The seven snapshot streams have neither a backfill nor an incremental leg in the intended sense: they are a full re-list of the whole collection every hour, with the CDK diffing the emitted byte stream to infer deletions and emit tombstones. Recorded under `backfill` with `incremental: null` because it is the bounded full pull, but 'backfill' implies a one-time catch-up that later hands off to an incremental leg, and no handoff ever happens here. This is also why parent-ID fan-out order is sorted: an unstable order would re-emit every child document each poll.

snapshot.deletionInference: digest of emitted byte stream; absent rows tombstoned

unionMisfits.description: The template variant fits the API-key path exactly but overstates the OAuth path. Under OAuth the connector does not substitute a {dc} into the template at all — it takes the `api_endpoint` string returned by https://login.mailchimp.com/oauth2/metadata and concatenates '/3.0'. The observed result happens to match the template, but the resolution is 'resolved', not 'template'. One connector therefore needs both baseUrl variants, selected by which credentialMode is active.

OAuth (long-lived access token).resolution: GET https://login.mailchimp.com/oauth2/metadata with the bearer token; use /api_endpoint verbatim and append '/3.0'

unionMisfits.description: pathPlaceholders (new in v2) captures WHICH ids fill each path segment, which is a real improvement, but it is a free-text description field, so the fan-out mechanics stay unmodeled: that the parent collection is drained with a fields=<items_key>.id projection, that it is fully materialized before any child request, that ids are sorted for determinism, that an empty id is rejected rather than templated, that two-level streams (interests, segment_members) chain two drains, and that for some children the parent id must additionally be stamped into _meta because the response omits it (tags, segment_members, automation_emails) while for others injecting it would be a duplicate (interest_categories, interests).

abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: The connector sets no headers of its own; the only header added is the CDK's Authorization. No API-version or revision header is sent — the version lives in the /3.0 path segment.
abstained.execution.schedule: There is no connector-level schedule. Cadence is entirely per-binding (ResourceConfigWithSchedule.interval), so the value is recorded on each stream and left null here.
abstained.discovery: Nothing is discovered from the customer's schema: the binding list is a fixed set of model classes assembled in all_resources(). The parent-ID fan-out (which lists/campaigns/automations exist) changes how many requests a static stream makes, not which streams exist, so it is recorded under pathPlaceholders rather than as discovery.
abstained.streams[7..10].writeDisposition: The connector never states merge-vs-append for the incremental bindings; Flow reduces by collection key, which behaves as a merge, but no code or config asserts it. Recorded as 'merge' on that inference alone.
abstained.streams[1].pull.backfill / streams[6].pu: The automations and automation_emails endpoints are feature-gated and returned empty on the test account, so their shapes (ITEMS_KEY, response fields, whether the response carries workflow_id) are docs-based and never live-verified. The connector's own docstrings say so.
abstained.streams[5].pull.backfill.paginator: tag-search is documented by Mailchimp WITHOUT offset/count support; the connector sends them anyway because they are observed to work. If the provider stops honouring them the walker silently degrades to a single page of up to 1000 tags and reports a clean sync. This is the one paginator here that could be wrong through no fault of the extraction.
abstained.streams[7].pull.*.params.before_create_t: Computed per invocation (last fully-elapsed second for the incremental leg, cutoff − 1s for the frozen backfill window), not literals. Recorded as described placeholders.
abstained.streams[8].cursorField: The emitted document's cursor is the flattened event's `timestamp`, but the checkpoint is max(emitted timestamp) and the NEXT poll rewinds it by a 10-minute LOOKBACK, deduping the overlap through an in-process cache. Campaign selection is gated on /reports recency fields (opens.last_open, clicks.last_click, send_time+bounce counts) rather than on the cursor. 'timestamp' is right for the document and understates the mechanism.
abstained.streams[8].pull.*.params: The exclude_fields default is what the shared page fetcher applies to the email-activity request, which is what is recorded. The `fields=reports.*` projection belongs to the /reports gate call — a different, unmodeled request — and is described under pathPlaceholders instead.
abstained.credentialModes[1].tier: Judgement call, not a fact in the source. The config schema requires client_id + client_secret + access_token standalone, which is strictly more work than T2_BYO_APP, but Mailchimp issues no refresh token so T3's literal 'refresh token' criterion is not met. Scored T3_BYO_REFRESH on equivalent user effort; a reviewer could defensibly call it T2.
abstained.rateLimits: No rate-limit, retry, backoff, or concurrency configuration is expressed anywhere in the connector. Mailchimp's documented 10-concurrent-request cap is not referenced. Whatever the CDK's HTTP layer does was not inspected.
abstained.streams[*].supportedSyncModes: Derived from whether the CDK resource is a SnapshotResource (full_refresh only) or opens with both fetch_changes and fetch_page (both modes). The connector never enumerates sync modes itself; the concept is Airbyte's, not Flow's.
